facts.statement: Mussaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur.
facts.quote: Mussaurus (meaning "mouse lizard") is a genus of herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur

facts.statement: The genus name Mussaurus means "mouse lizard" because early discoveries consisted only of small juvenile skeletons.
facts.quote: It receives its name from the small size of the skeletons of juvenile and infant individuals, which were once the only known specimens of the genus.

facts.statement: Juvenile Mussaurus were small quadrupedal herbivores that walked on all four legs.
facts.quote: In its early stages of life, Mussaurus was a small quadrupedal herbivore, walking on all four legs.

facts.statement: Adult Mussaurus were medium-sized bipedal herbivores reaching up to 8 meters in length and weighing between 1.2 and 1.6 metric tons.
facts.quote: Adults would have been medium-sized bipedal herbivores, measuring up to 8 m long and weighing up to 1.2 - 1.6 MT.

facts.statement: Multiple specimens of different ages found together suggest Mussaurus lived in a gregarious lifestyle.
facts.quote: Numerous specimens of varying age found in a single locality suggest that Mussaurus is one of the earliest dinosaurs to have lived in a gregarious lifestyle.

facts.statement: The discovery team found fossilized eggs and hatchlings, providing insight into the reproductive strategies of Mussaurus.
facts.quote: The team found fossilized eggs and hatchlings, which added insight into the reproductive strategies of Mussaurus and other sauropodomorph dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The first adult specimens of Mussaurus were formally described in 2013, though some were initially described in 1980 under the genus Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: The first adult specimens of Mussaurus were described in 2013, although some of these specimens had first been described in 1980 and were originally attributed to the genus Plateosaurus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Mussaurus have been found in association with nests believed to contain multiple eggs.
facts.quote: Mussaurus specimens have been found in association with nests that are believed to contain multiple eggs apiece.

facts.statement: Mussaurus infant skeletons measured about 20 cm in length and weighed between 53.3 and 76.5 grams.
facts.quote: The skeletons of Mussaurus infants were small, measuring about 20 cm long and weighing about 53.3 - 76.5 g.

facts.statement: Researchers initially reported evidence of medullary bone in a Mussaurus specimen in 2013, but later argued in 2014 that the tissue was likely pathological.
facts.quote: Ignacio Cerda and Diego Pol reported putative evidence of medullary bone tissue from a specimen of Mussaurus in 2013, but both authors with Anusuya Chinsamy subsequently argued in 2014 that this tissue most likely represents a pathologically formed tissue instead based on histological features.

facts.statement: As of 2021, Mussaurus holds the record for the earliest unequivocal evidence of complex social behavior in dinosaurs, with over 100 eggs and 80 individuals found in one locality.
facts.quote: As of 2021, Mussaurus represents the earliest unequivocal evidence of complex social behaviour in dinosaurs, with over 100 eggs and skeletal specimens of 80 individuals ranging from embryos to adults found in the same locality.

facts.statement: Juvenile Mussaurus had short skulls and necks, long tails, and large eye sockets.
facts.quote: Los juveniles tenían el cráneo y el cuello cortos, la cola larga y grandes fosas oculares.

facts.statement: Adult specimens indicate that Mussaurus likely had longer necks and reached a maximum length of 6 meters and a weight of 1000 kilograms.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, posteriormente se han encontrado especímenes adultos de este género, con lo que se ha podido determinar que los adultos tendrían cuellos más largos y probablemente alcanzaron como máximo 6 metros de largo, con un peso de 1000 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Mussaurus lived during the late Triassic, approximately 215 million years ago in the Norian stage in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 215 millones de años, en el Noriense, en lo que hoy es América del Sur.

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in 1976 by an expedition led by José Fernando Bonaparte in the El Tranquilo Formation of Santa Cruz Province.
facts.quote: Los fósiles fueron descubiertos por una expedición liderada por José Fernando Bonaparte durante el año de 1976 en la Formación El Tranquilo de la Provincia de Santa Cruz.

facts.statement: The expedition team found fossilized eggs and nests that revealed the reproductive strategies of Mussaurus and other prosauropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: El equipo encontró los huevos y nidos fosilizados, que revelaron las estrategias reproductivas de Mussaurus y otros dinosaurios prosaurópodos.

facts.statement: Mussaurus was initially classified as an incertae sedis sauropodomorph because it could be either a prosauropod or a primitive sauropod.
facts.quote: Mussaurus se clasificó inicialmente como un sauropodomorfo incertae sedis, ya que podría tratarse tanto de un prosaurópodo como de un saurópodo primitivo.

facts.statement: In 1980, Dr. Rodolfo Casamiquela published an article relating adult specimens to the European genus Plateosaurus within the family Plateosauridae.
facts.quote: El Dr. Rodolfo Casamiquela publicó en 1980 un artículo sobre los especímenes adultos de estos saurópodos y los relacionó con el género europeo Plateosaurus, dentro de Plateosauridae.

facts.statement: Anatomical features suggest Mussaurus was close to the possible direct ancestor of true sauropods.
facts.quote: Mussaurus posee características anatómicas que sugieren que se encontraba cerca del posible antepasado directo de los verdaderos saurópodos.

facts.statement: Mussaurus is estimated to have reached sexual maturity between 23 and 31 years of age and somatic maturity after 14 years.
facts.quote: It is estimated that Mussaurus would have been sexually mature at 23 to 31 years of age, and reached somatic maturity after 14 years.

facts.statement: Fossils of Mussaurus have been found associated with nests believed to contain multiple eggs each.
facts.quote: Los especímenes de Mussaurus se han encontrado en asociación con nidos que se creen que contenían cada uno múltiples huevos.

facts.statement: Baby Mussaurus skeletons were small, measuring only 20 centimeters without the tail and 37 centimeters with it, similar in size to a small lizard.
facts.quote: El esqueleto de las crías de Mussaurus eran pequeños, de sólo 20 centímetros sin la cola y 37 con ella, siendo similar al tamaño de un pequeño lagarto.

facts.statement: Like many juvenile dinosaurs, Mussaurus had high skulls with short snouts and large eyes.
facts.quote: Al igual que como es común en los dinosaurios juveniles, Mussaurus tenía cráneos altos con los hocicos cortos y los ojos grandes.

facts.statement: Juveniles of Mussaurus differed from adults in their body proportions, in addition to size and weight differences.
facts.quote: Los jóvenes se diferencian de adultos en sus proporciones además de la diferencia de tamaño y peso.

facts.statement: Adult Mussaurus had longer snouts and necks and would have looked more like a typical prosauropod.
facts.quote: Los adultos por su parte tenían hocicos y cuellos más largos, y se verían más parecidos a un prosaurópodo típico.

facts.statement: A study published in May 2019 suggests that while M. patagonicus was quadrupedal during its first year of life, changes in body proportions during growth shifted its center of mass backward, causing it to adopt a bipedal posture later in life.
facts.quote: Un estudio publicado en mayo de 2019 muestra que, aunque M. patagonicus probablemente caminó sobre las cuatro extremidades, era cuadrúpedo, durante el primer año de su vida, los cambios en las proporciones relativas de su cuerpo durante el crecimiento, ontogenia, hicieron que su centro de masa se moviera hacia atrás, hacia su pelvis, lo que hace que el animal adopte una postura de dos patas, bípedo, más adelante en la vida.

facts.statement: A 2007 paper by Pol and Powell described the skull anatomy of Mussaurus patagonicus from the Late Triassic of Patagonia.
facts.quote: Pol, D. & Powell, J. E. 2007. Skull anatomy of Mussaurus patagonicus (Dinosauria: Sauropodomorpha) from the Late Triassic of Patagonia. Historical Biology, 19, 1, 125-144.

facts.statement: The genus Mussaurus belongs to the parent group Sauropodiformes.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropodiformes

facts.statement: Mussaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Mussaurus lived from 199.5 to 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Infant and juvenile fossils of Mussaurus were first discovered in the 1970s by an expedition led by Jose Bonaparte in the Laguna Colorada Formation.
rejected.quote: Infant and juvenile fossils of Mussaurus were first discovered by an expedition led by Jose Bonaparte during the 1970s to the Laguna Colorada Formation

rejected.quote: As is common for dinosaurs, juvenile Mussaurus had tall skulls with short snouts and large eyes.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'tall skulls with short snouts and large eyes'

rejected.statement: The discovery of herd-living Mussaurus predates previous records of herd-living dinosaurs by at least 40 million years.
rejected.quote: This discovery predates the previous records of herd-living dinosaurs by at least 40 million years.
